final.title: Synthetic test data: a workflow decision, not a project
final.body:
Synthetic test data is only worth the effort when it helps you make a workflow decision faster. For a small business, the real question is simpler: are you building test data because you need privacy or scale, or because nobody has tried the workflow on real records yet?

For one repeatable process, like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start smaller. Use a limited real-data subset, clear rules, and human approval anywhere money or another high-risk decision is involved. That keeps the work focused on the workflow, not on the theatre of perfect fake data.

Bareni’s accounts-payable demo is a useful boundary case. It uses entirely synthetic data to show the mechanics: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But it also has limits. The default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion and OCR are not implemented. So it shows control logic, not a claim that it can handle every real invoice pile.

My practical next step would be to pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of actual records, then test whether synthetic data is solving a real problem or just delaying the moment you learn what the workflow needs. If it is the second one, the spreadsheet has already won.
